title: Vue Router and Pinia: choose where state lives
outcome: Use URL state, component state, and stores deliberately, including route changes and server rendering.
drawbacks: Stores can become dumping grounds without ownership rules.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: URL for context. Store for sharing. Server for authority.

trace.title: URL context
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A route is part of the user’s working context. Search, selected workspace, and page often need to survive refresh or be shared.

Put those values in a stable URL contract and parse them, including invalid inputs.

A store is useful for shared application state and named actions. It does not automatically solve server cache freshness.

Keep remote data, local drafts, and permissions separate. With Pinia, storeToRefs preserves reactivity when destructuring state/getters; actions can be called from the store normally.

Route components can be reused when params change. Watching only onMounted can leave the old ticket on screen after navigation.

Watch the relevant ID or use a deliberate route data-loading strategy. A navigation guard improves UX but the server must still enforce access.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Direct URL → parse query/params → establish workspace context → load allowed server data → render → user changes filter → update URL. Back navigation should restore meaningful state.

For an unsaved form, define whether navigation prompts, saves a draft, or discards it. Browser Back and an in-app link should follow the same user-facing policy.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
A single global editing object can make two open panes overwrite each other. A route guard is not server authorization.

Query-string arrays and absent values require parsing.
